content.text:
I've read all five specs, installed the real Entire CLI (v0.10.5) and reverse-engineered its checkpoint model against a scratch repo, inventoried the environment, and verified the Databricks/MCP/Python-3.14 dependency picture. Full audit below.

---

# DevMemory — Deep Project Audit & Implementation Strategy

## 1. Executive Assessment

**What we are building:** a reusable, `pip`-installable Python platform (`devmemory`) that sits *beside* a developer's existing tools and turns each meaningful AI-assisted change into a **Development Version** — a durable record that stitches together five otherwise-disconnected facts:

| Layer | Owner | DevMemory's job |
|---|---|---|
| *What* changed (commit, diff, files, renames, line counts) | **Git** | reference + cache |
| *Why / who / how* (prompt, agent, model, transcript, tokens) | **Entire checkpoint** | reference + normalize |
| *What resulted* (tests, metrics, regressions, status) | **DevMemory** | own it |
| *What it means* (analysis, recommendation, previous-attempt warnings) | **DevMemory intelligence** (LLM) | own it, kept separate from facts |
| *What the trend is* (cross-version analytics, agent/feature/file intelligence) | **Databricks** | analytics layer |

Consumed two ways: a **visual dashboard** for humans and an **MCP server + REST context API** for the next AI agent. The unique, defensible core is the *join*, not any single node — and the join is only credible if the Entire checkpoint is a first-class, real (never fabricated) participant.

**Verdict on feasibility:** high. Every integration point is real and reachable on this machine. The Entire checkpoint↔commit link is a plain Git trailer we can read without Entire even running; the Entire CLI gives clean `--json` on top; Databricks has a REST-only path that needs no Spark; Python 3.14 resolves the whole stack. There are no blocking unknowns — only sequencing discipline.

---

## 2. Current Repository State

```
D:\Hackathons\TechWeek\
└── docs\
    ├── PROJECT_SPEC.md          (1683 lines)
    ├── ARCHITECTURE.md          (2687 lines)
    ├── ENTIRE_QUICKSTART.md     (a.k.a. "Entire Integration Reference", 1365 lines)
    ├── ENTIRE_INTEGRATION.md    ("Entire Integration Specification", 905 lines)
    └── DATA_AND_API_SPEC.md     (1819 lines)
```

- **Not a Git repository.** No `.git`, no `.devmemory`, no `.entire`, no `.claude`, no `pyproject.toml`, no source, no frontend. Greenfield.
- Docs are extensive, internally consistent, and unusually prescriptive (they repeatedly say "inspect the real tool, don't guess" — which I did).
- The five docs overlap ~40%. `PROJECT_SPEC` = product; `ARCHITECTURE` = system design + build order; the two Entire docs = near-duplicates of the same integration guidance; `DATA_AND_API_SPEC` = schema + endpoints + MCP tools.

---

## 3. Environment

| Tool | Version | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| OS | Windows 11 Home (26200) | PowerShell 5.1 primary; Git Bash available |
| Python | **3.14.6** (python.org, `C:\Users\BANU\AppData\Local\Python`) | single global env, **no venv** |
| pip | 26.1.2 | has `pip-tools`, `build`; **no `uv`, no `pipx`** |
| Git | 2.47.1.windows.1 | `core.autocrlf` unset → CRLF warnings; `user.name=Banu`, `user.email=banubb2005@gmail.com` (note: differs from account email), no commit signing |
| Node | 22.12.0 / npm 10.9.2 | fine for a Vite build step |
| Go | 1.27.0 | used it to install Entire |
| Docker | 28.5.2 | present, not needed for MVP |
| SQLite (via Python) | **3.50.4**, FTS5 ✅, JSON1 ✅ | full-text search + `json_extract` available out of the box |
| Entire | **not installed** → I installed **0.10.5** to `C:\Users\BANU\go\bin\entire.exe` | see §4 |

**Global Python packages already present that matter:** `pydantic 2.13.4`, `httpx 0.28.1`, `openai 2.52.0`, `google-genai 2.15.0` / `google-generativeai 0.8.6`, `requests`, `PyYAML`, `python-dotenv`, `redis`, `celery`, full Django/DRF stack.
**Absent (must be added, in a venv):** `fastapi`, `uvicorn`, `typer`, `pytest`, `databricks-sdk`, `mcp`/`fastmcp`, `jinja2`, `structlog`, `rich`.

**Credentials:** `~/.claude/.credentials.json` exists (Claude Code OAuth). **No** `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, or `DATABRICKS_*` environment variables are set.

**Dependency resolution on 3.14 (dry-run, all resolve):** `fastapi 0.141.1`, `uvicorn 0.52.4`, `typer 0.27.2`, `databricks-sdk 0.135.0`, `fastmcp 4.0.3` (or `mcp 2.1.1`), `pytest 9.1.1`, `structlog 26.1.0`, `rich 15.0.0`, `jinja2 3.1.6`. Python 3.14 is **not** a risk — the ecosystem has caught up (it's Sept 2026).

**Things I changed / created (all outside the project):**
- Installed `entire.exe` (~66 MB) to `C:\Users\BANU\go\bin`, plus ~450 MB Go build/module cache in `C:\Users\BANU\AppData\Local\go-build` and `go\pkg\mod`. Removable with `go clean -cache -modcache` and deleting the binary.
- Imported **1 read-only Entire checkpoint** into a throwaway repo under the session scratchpad (auto-cleaned). Nothing touched the real project.

---

## 4. Entire Analysis (verified against installed CLI 0.10.5)

### 4.1 Install & shape
- Go binary. `go install github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire@latest`, or `irm https://entire.io/install.ps1 | iex` on Windows, or `brew` on mac. Self-updates via `entire plugin install upgrade`.
- Agent-agnostic: `claude-code`, `codex`, `copilot-cli`, `cursor`, `factoryai-droid`, `gemini`, `opencode`, `pi` + external agents on `$PATH`.
- **Fully local, no login required** for capture, checkpoint reads, `why`, `blame`, `explain`. Login (`entire login`, GitHub device flow) is needed only for: hosted dashboard sync, `entire search` (semantic), `entire recap` / `entire activity` (hosted views), cross-repo `explain --repo`.

### 4.2 What `entire enable --agent claude-code --yes --no-github` produces
```
.entire/settings.json     (committed)  {"enabled":true,"telemetry":..,"checkpoints":{"primary":{"type":"git-refs"}}}
.entire/.gitignore                      ignores tmp/ settings.local.json metadata/ logs/ redactors/local/
.claude/settings.json     (committed)  8 hooks → `entire hooks claude-code <phase>`
.git/hooks/prepare-commit-msg          injects `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer at commit time
.git/hooks/commit-msg                  strips trailer if commit has no real content
.git/hooks/post-commit                 condenses session data when trailer present
.git/hooks/post-rewrite                remaps checkpoint linkage after amend/rebase/squash
.git/hooks/pre-push                    pushes session logs alongside your push
```
All hooks are `command -v entire`-guarded (no-op if Entire absent). In this version linking is **automatic and non-interactive** by default (the "[Y]es/[n]o/[a]lways" prompt in older docs corresponds to a `commit_linking` setting that isn't written by default).

### 4.3 Checkpoint storage — the data model (read directly from Git objects)
Backend `git-refs` (default): one ref per checkpoint at **`refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>`** where `<shard>` = last 2 chars of the id. (Legacy backend: a shared `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch.)

Each ref → a commit whose tree is:
```
metadata.json                 top-level envelope
<idx>/metadata.json           per-session metadata
<idx>/prompt.txt              ← the user's prompt  == INTENT
<idx>/full.jsonl              full transcript
<idx>/transcript.jsonl        compact transcript
<idx>/content_hash.txt
```

```json
{ "cli_version":"0.10.5", "checkpoint_id":"8149ec99eeae", "strategy":"import",
  "commit_sha":"9c714eb...", "checkpoints_count":1, "files_touched":null,
  "sessions":[{"metadata":"/0/metadata.json","transcript":"/0/full.jsonl",

  "token_usage":{"input_tokens":72,"cache_creation_tokens":150510,

```
Per-session `<idx>/metadata.json` adds: `session_id`, `agent` ("Claude Code"), `model` ("claude-sonnet-5"), `created_at` (ISO-8601), `kind` ("imported" | live), transcript offsets, `token_usage`.

**Checkpoint IDs:** 26-char ULID for hook-captured checkpoints; 12-char hex for imported/logs-only.

### 4.4 Commit ↔ checkpoint association — verified, three layers
1. **Git trailer (primary, no Entire dependency):**
   `git show -s --format='%(trailers:key=Entire-Checkpoint,valueonly)' <sha>` → `8149ec99eeae`
   Trailer survives rebase/amend/squash/cherry-pick (it's stored, not derived from the hash).
2. **Entire CLI resolution (context):**
   `entire checkpoint explain --commit <sha> --json` → metadata envelope (no transcript bytes)
   `entire checkpoint explain <id> --json` → same, by id
   `entire checkpoint explain <id> --transcript` → JSONL transcript stream
   `entire checkpoint list --json` → `[{checkpoint_id, session_id, agent, date, message, is_logs_only, session_count, session_ids[]}]`
3. **Direct Git object read (offline fallback):**
   `git cat-file -p refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>:metadata.json` and `:<idx>/prompt.txt`
   Works with zero Entire involvement — this is our resilience story.

Per-file / per-line AI attribution (verified `--json` schemas):
`entire why <file>[:line] --json` and `entire blame <file>[:range] --json` →
`{file, lines:[{line_number, authorship:"human|ai|mixed", tag:"[HU]|[AI]|[MX]", commit_sha, author, author_time, content}], summary:{total_lines, ai_lines, ai_percentage, ...}}`

### 4.5 Getting real checkpoints for the demo — three paths
- **Live (best):** run Claude Code in a repo that has `entire enable` + `.claude/settings.json` hooks. Hooks capture the session; the commit gets a ULID checkpoint + trailer automatically. Since the user *is* driving Claude Code in VS Code, our own dogfooding on the demo repo produces genuine checkpoints.
- **`entire session attach <session-id> --force`** (verified): builds a checkpoint from an existing transcript and **amends HEAD with the trailer**. This is the essential recovery path when hooks didn't fire (e.g. a session that started before enable).
- **`entire import claude-code [--path DIR]`** (verified): bulk-imports past transcripts as **read-only, non-commit-linked** checkpoints. Good for back-filling history/search; *not* for the trailer flow.

### 4.6 `entire status --json` (verified)
`{"enabled":true,"agents":["Claude Code"],"active_sessions":[],"agent_help":"entire agent-help"}`

### 4.7 `entire agent-help [command]` — machine-readable usage that "always matches the installed CLI." Our adapter should treat `entire agent-help` + `--json` as the contract and never hard-code flags.

### 4.8 Limitations / gotchas
- **Repo auto-detection needs an `origin` remote** (or it says "pass `--repo`"). Detached HEAD also breaks detection. Our adapter must pass `--repo` explicitly or ensure the demo repo has an origin.
- `entire checkpoint explain` metadata JSON **excludes intent/prompt text** in the envelope — you get `sessions[]` metadata only. For intent, read `<idx>/prompt.txt` from the ref, or `entire checkpoint list --json` `message` field, or `--short` (human text, not JSON). **Recommendation:** read `prompt.txt` from the Git object for a clean, structured intent string.
- Imported checkpoints are `is_logs_only:true`, `kind:"imported"`, no rewind. Mark association method accordingly.
- Secret redaction is best-effort (betterleaks/goredact) *inside Entire*. We still must not re-surface transcript content into Databricks/dashboard/SQLite beyond references + short prompt.
- CRLF: Git on this machine rewrites LF→CRLF; keep a `.gitattributes` in generated repos and normalize when hashing.

### Recommended Entire implementation
`adapters/entire.py` exposes only normalized types. Resolution order per commit:
`trailer (git) → explain --commit --json (context, confidence=1.0, method="trailer") → direct ref read (offline, confidence=1.0, method="git-ref") → entire checkpoint list --json time/branch match (confidence≤0.6, method="heuristic", UI-flagged) → none (entire_status:"unavailable", never fabricated)`.
Subprocess wrapper: locate binary (`shutil.which`, then `~/go/bin`, then config override), `entire version` gate, per-call timeout, `--json` always, structured error taxonomy (`ENTIRE_ABSENT`, `ENTIRE_DISABLED`, `NO_CHECKPOINT`, `AMBIGUOUS`, `CLI_ERROR`).

## 5. Git Analysis

Pure subprocess, no GitPython (keeps deps minimal, behaves identically across platforms). Rules:
- Invoke with explicit `cwd`, `env` including `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, `--no-pager`.
- `pathlib.Path` everywhere; never string-concat paths; POSIX-normalize stored file paths.
- Parse `-z` NUL-delimited output where available (`diff --name-status -z`, `for-each-ref`).

| Need | Command |
|---|---|
| repo root | `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` |
| current commit / branch | `git rev-parse HEAD` / `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` |
| parent | `git rev-parse HEAD^` (handle root commit → `null`) |
| commit meta | `git show -s --format=%H%x00%P%x00%an%x00%ae%x00%aI%x00%B HEAD` |
| Entire trailer | `git show -s --format='%(trailers:key=Entire-Checkpoint,valueonly)' HEAD` |
| changed files + status + renames | `git diff --name-status -M -z <parent> <commit>` |
| line stats per file | `git diff --numstat -z <parent> <commit>` (binary → `-\t-`) |
| full diff (display) | `git diff <parent> <commit>` (+ `--stat` summary) |
| dirty check (restore safety) | `git status --porcelain=v2 -z` |
| snapshot | `git archive --format=tar <commit>` piped to Python `tarfile` for filtering |
| restore | `git switch --detach <commit>` after safety tag `git tag devmemory/safety/<ts>` |

Diffs are **generated on demand** from the two commits (source of truth) and only *cached* in SQLite for dashboard speed, with the commit pair always stored so any diff can be recomputed.

## 6. Databricks Analysis

**Recommended integration — REST-only, no Spark, no cluster:**
- `databricks-sdk` → **SQL Statement Execution API** (`w.statement_execution.execute_statement`) against a **serverless SQL warehouse**. Works on Databricks **Free Edition**. Auth from env only: `DATABRICKS_HOST`, `DATABRICKS_TOKEN`, `DATABRICKS_WAREHOUSE_ID` (+ optional `DATABRICKS_CATALOG`, `DATABRICKS_SCHEMA`).
- On first `databricks push`: `CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS devmemory` + `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` for a **star-ish schema**: `dim_projects`, `fact_versions`, `fact_changed_files`, `fact_tests`, `fact_metrics`, `fact_regressions`, `dim_features`, `dim_checkpoints`, `dim_agent_sessions`.
- `DatabricksAdapter.publish_version(v)` → idempotent `MERGE INTO fact_versions ... WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT` keyed on `(project_id, version_id)`; child rows delete-then-insert per version. **Never** send transcript bodies or full source — only normalized fields + short intent.
- **Offline-first:** if unreachable, write the event to `.devmemory/outbox/<version>.json`; `devmemory databricks push` (and a dashboard "Sync" button) drains it. Local history never depends on the cloud.

**Making it *meaningful* (not "integration complete"):** ship a set of canned analytical queries wired to a dashboard **"Intelligence"** tab and to MCP:
- regression leaderboard (versions, feature, metric delta, severity)
- feature attempt-count & success-rate over time
- most-frequently-changed files (churn) joined to regression incidence
- agent/session success rate & token cost per successful change
- rolling test-pass-rate and key-metric trend lines
- "approaches that repeatedly failed" (cluster by changed-file set + intent keywords + REGRESSION)

**Agent observability (stretch, not MVP):** optionally emit one **MLflow trace** per version (`intent → agent/model → tokens → files → tests → status`) to the same workspace's MLflow, so the "AI agent → prompt → tools → result" trace is inspectable in Databricks. One clean trace beats a half-built observability platform.

**Risk:** requires the user to create a free workspace + PAT + serverless warehouse. If they won't, the whole Databricks slice degrades gracefully to "local analytics computed from SQLite with the identical query semantics," and the dashboard shows both with a source badge.

## 9. Architecture Review

The docs' architecture is sound. Changes I'd make:

1. **`src/` layout + `hatchling`**, single package `devmemory`. Keep the doc's module tree but **collapse premature splits**: `collectors/` folds into a single `pipeline.py` (the checkpoint pipeline is one ordered thing); `intelligence/` keeps `analyzer.py` + `regression.py` + `memory.py` + `features.py`.
2. **No SQLAlchemy.** Stdlib `sqlite3` + a hand-written repository layer + a tiny numbered-migrations runner. SQLite 3.50 here has FTS5 + JSON1. This removes a heavy dependency for zero real benefit at this scale and keeps queries transparent.
3. **Domain services layer is the single waist.** CLI, REST, and MCP are all thin adapters over `devmemory.services.*`. Nothing but `services` and `storage` touches SQLite.
4. **Adapters return normalized Pydantic models only.** `EntireAdapter`, `GitAdapter`, `TestAdapter`, `MetricsAdapter`, `DatabricksAdapter`, `GraphAdapter`, `AnalysisProvider` (LLM abstraction: Anthropic via Claude Code OAuth or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, OpenAI, Gemini, or `none` → rule-based only).
5. **Frontend: Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind, pre-built into static assets shipped inside the wheel.** `devmemory serve` serves the built bundle + FastAPI JSON — **no Node at runtime**, `pip install devmemory` is enough. This is the only way to hit "visually impressive" without a runtime build step. (Fallback if we want zero-JS-build: server-rendered Jinja + hand-rolled SVG charts — less impressive, keep as Plan B.)
6. **Explicit "facts vs analysis" boundary in the schema** (separate `analysis` table, never written by collectors; API responses tag every field's source). ARCHITECTURE §25 and DATA_AND_API_SPEC §16 demand this — make it structural, not a convention.
7. **`run_id` + structured run log per `devmemory checkpoint`** so §22 observability ("what failed, which integration, was project state changed, what next") is answerable. Each pipeline stage records `{stage, status, duration, error, degraded}`.
8. **Config precedence:** `.devmemory/config.json` (committed, non-secret) → `.devmemory/config.local.json` (gitignored) → env vars (secrets only) → CLI flags. Mirror Entire's own `settings.json` / `settings.local.json` split so it feels native.

|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Demo has no genuine Entire checkpoints** (hooks don't fire mid-session; the current Claude Code session predates any enable) | **HIGH** | Enable Entire early in the demo repo; dogfood real sessions; `entire session attach --force` as the deterministic backfill; `entire import` for history. Rehearse the exact sequence. |
| 2 | Entire needs `origin` remote for repo auto-detection | MED | Adapter always passes `--repo`; demo repo gets a GitHub origin (or `entire enable` creates one). |
| 3 | Entire CLI output/flags change (pre-1.0, v0.10.5) | MED | Only use `--json`; treat `entire agent-help` as contract; direct Git-object fallback path; pin nothing but detect version and adapt. |
| 4 | Databricks account/warehouse not provisioned in time | MED | Local-SQLite analytics with identical query semantics + source badge; outbox drains later. |
| 5 | LLM analysis unavailable (no API key) | MED | `AnalysisProvider="none"` → deterministic rule-based summary/recommendation; UI clearly labels "heuristic". |
| 6 | Python 3.14 wheel gaps | LOW | Verified full resolution today; still pin a lockfile and support 3.11–3.14. |
| 7 | Restore corrupts uncommitted work | MED | Refuse on dirty tree without `--force`; safety tag + `git stash create` ref before any state change; detached-checkout preview mode is the default, destructive reset is a separate explicit command. |
| 8 | CRLF changes file hashes / diffs on Windows | LOW | `.gitattributes` + `-c core.autocrlf=false` for internal git calls; hash normalized bytes. |
| 9 | Checkpoint idempotency / double-`checkpoint` | LOW | Unique `(project_id, git_commit)`; detect + report existing version; `--force` to supersede. |
| 10 | Frontend build adds friction to `pip install` | LOW | Commit built assets; wheel ships them; CI rebuilds. Node only for devs of DevMemory itself. |

## 12. Security Risks

- **Secrets:** only from env / `config.local.json` (gitignored). Never in SQLite, Git trailers, dashboard HTML, API responses, Databricks rows, logs. A `redact()` pass on all log records and a startup check that `config.local.json` is gitignored.
- **Transcript/source exfiltration:** DevMemory stores checkpoint **references + short prompt excerpt** only; full transcripts stay in Entire's refs. Databricks receives normalized telemetry only — a hard allowlist of fields, enforced in `DatabricksAdapter`, not by convention.
- **Dashboard is localhost-only, unauthenticated** by design; bind `127.0.0.1`; document that remote exposure needs auth (out of MVP scope). `POST /restore` disabled unless `--enable-restore` given to `serve`.
- **LLM calls:** send diff + metrics + intent; never send env/secret files; respect a configurable path denylist; note in docs that analysis text goes to the configured model provider.
- **Subprocess:** no `shell=True`; arg lists only; validated commit SHAs (`^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$`) and checkpoint ids before interpolation.
- `entire`'s own redaction is best-effort — we treat prompt excerpts as potentially sensitive and truncate + store locally only.

## 13. Cross-Platform Risks

- **Primary target is Windows** (this machine) but package must be OS-neutral: `pathlib` only, `subprocess` arg-lists, `sys.executable` for re-invocation, `tarfile`/`zipfile` from stdlib (not shelling `tar`), `os.replace` for atomic writes, `platformdirs` for any cache outside the repo.
- Git line endings (see risk #8).
- Path separators in stored `changed_files` → always POSIX.
- Shell in Entire's generated hooks is `sh` (Git Bash) — fine here; document that Git for Windows must be installed (it is).
- FastAPI/uvicorn on Windows: use the default `asyncio` loop (no `uvloop`), `--reload` off in the shipped server.
- Test suite runs on Windows CI + Linux CI.

## 16. Implementation Phases

Each phase ends with a **working vertical slice** + tests + a demo-able command. Ordering refined from the docs by real dependencies.

**Phase 0 — Foundation (repo + package skeleton)**
`git init`; `pyproject.toml`; `devmemory --version`/`--help`; config loader; structlog; error taxonomy; migrations runner; CI green; `docs/IMPLEMENTATION_STRATEGY.md` committed. `entire enable` on this repo so we generate real checkpoints from here on.

**Phase 1 — `init` + config + Git adapter**
`devmemory init` → `.devmemory/`, SQLite schema, project row, environment detection, Entire/agent detection summary. `GitAdapter` complete + unit-tested against `tmp_path` repos.

**Phase 2 — Entire adapter (the pillar)**
Trailer read → `explain --commit --json` → direct git-ref read → heuristic → none. Normalized `CheckpointReference` with method/confidence/prompt-excerpt. Tests use recorded `--json` payloads + a real `entire enable`d fixture repo.

**Phase 3 — `DevelopmentEvent` normalization + `DevelopmentVersion` registry + SQLite persistence**
The join happens here. Version numbering, idempotency `(project, commit)`, `versions/vN.json` mirror.

**Phase 4 — `devmemory checkpoint` (end-to-end, no results yet)**
The 19-step pipeline with per-stage run log. `--allow-no-entire`, `--feature`, `--intent`, `--force`. `devmemory status` / `history` / `show vN` (Rich output).
→ **Milestone 1:** real commit + real Entire checkpoint → Version created, visible in CLI.

**Phase 5 — REST API + dashboard shell**
FastAPI routes for project/status/versions/version-detail/diff/checkpoint. Vite/React app: Overview, Timeline, Version Detail, **Development Trace** (intent→agent→checkpoint→commit→files→diff). `devmemory serve`.
→ **Milestone 2:** `devmemory serve` shows the version with its full trace + real Git diff + real checkpoint.

**Phase 6 — Tests + metrics + status + regression**
Configurable `test_command` runner (pytest/npm/go/…): capture exit/stdout/stderr/duration + parse counts (pytest & junit-xml first). Metrics from JSON file / command / CLI input, direction-aware. `status_rules` + `regression` + `regressions` table. Feature detection + feature history pages.
→ **Milestone 3:** SUCCESS / REGRESSION computed from real evidence; feature evolution visible.

**Phase 7 — Development memory + previous attempts**
FTS5 index; `memory.get_previous_attempts(files|feature|intent|metric)`; ranking (exact file overlap → feature → intent keywords → failed/regressed). CLI `devmemory memory`; dashboard "Previous Attempts" + inline warnings on Version Detail.
→ **Milestone 4:** failed `learning_rate` (or token-expiry) approach is remembered and surfaced.

**Phase 8 — Version comparison + search**
`compare vA vB` service + `/api/compare` + Compare page (files, ±lines, metric deltas, test deltas, status/feature changes, real diff). Global search page.

**Phase 9 — Artifacts + safe restore**
`git archive`→`tar.gz` + env metadata; `artifacts` table. Restore: dirty-tree refusal, safety tag + stash ref, detached preview default, explicit `devmemory restore vN --hard`. Dashboard restore flow with the exact warning text from the spec. `/restore` gated behind `serve --enable-restore`.

**Phase 10 — Databricks**
Schema bootstrap; `DatabricksAdapter.publish_version` MERGE; outbox + `databricks push`; `analytics` service with canned queries (local-SQLite parity implementation); dashboard **Intelligence** tab.
→ **Milestone 5:** versions flow to Delta; regression leaderboard / feature-attempts / file-churn answered by real queries.

**Phase 11 — AI context API + MCP**
`context` service → `/api/context`; `fastmcp` server with all tools + `check_before_change`; `devmemory mcp install` writes `.mcp.json`. 
→ **Milestone 6:** a fresh Claude Code session calls DevMemory MCP and gets the same memory the dashboard shows.

**Phase 12 — Entire Graph / impact**
`entire plugin install graph` detection; `GraphAdapter.impact()`; Impact panel + `get_development_trace` enrichment; degrade gracefully.

**Phase 13 — AI analysis layer**
`AnalysisProvider` (Anthropic/OpenAI/Gemini/rules). Analysis strictly separate table + `source:"analysis"` tags. Numeric-claim guard (analysis may not contradict collected facts — validated).

**Phase 14 — Polish & integration**
`examples/demo-project` + `seed_history.py`; `devmemory doctor`; e2e test (commit→checkpoint→serve→context); dark/light theme; empty/error states; `DEMO.md` runbook; README with the real quickstart; screenshots.

---

## 17. Test Strategy

- **Unit:** Git parsing (renames, root commit, binary files, CRLF), Entire trailer/JSON/gitref parsing (recorded fixtures), status rules (table-driven), regression direction logic, feature detection, version numbering & idempotency, FTS ranking, repositories, config precedence, secret redaction, Databricks SQL builders (assert allowlist), artifact filter excludes.
- **Integration:** real temp Git repo fixture; a real `entire enable`d fixture repo with an attached imported checkpoint (checked into `tests/fixtures` as a bare repo); full `checkpoint` pipeline; FastAPI routes via `TestClient`; MCP tools via in-process client; restore safety (dirty tree, safety tag created, preview vs hard).
- **E2E:** scripted `init → commit → checkpoint → serve(API) → context/MCP` asserting the trace is consistent across all three surfaces; run on Windows + Linux CI.
- **Contract tests for Entire:** a nightly/optional job that runs against the *live* installed CLI and diffs the `--json` shape against our recorded fixtures — early warning on CLI drift.
- **Not automated (manual runbook in DEMO.md):** live Claude Code session producing a ULID checkpoint; Databricks against a real workspace; `entire graph` on a real index.
- Coverage target: 85%+ on `domain/`, `services/`, `pipeline/`, `adapters/git.py`, `adapters/entire*.py`.

---

## 18. Demo Strategy (the strongest end-to-end story)

**Repo:** `examples/demo-project` — a small non-ML web app (task API + auth + calculator, ~150 lines, real pytest suite). Deliberately not ML, to prove the "not everything is accuracy%" claim; metrics = test pass-rate + endpoint latency + error count.

**Pre-seeded history** (`seed_history.py` makes real commits; where a real transcript isn't available it uses `entire session attach` on genuine prior Claude Code transcripts — never fabricated):
- V1 SUCCESS — initial auth + task API
- V2 SUCCESS — add task filtering (latency 210→180 ms)
- V3 **REGRESSION** — "shorten JWT expiry to 30s" → 6 tests fail, error count ↑
- V4 SUCCESS — fix expiry handling (refresh window) → tests green

**Live on stage:**
1. In VS Code, ask Claude Code: *"make token expiry configurable and safe."* Entire captures the session (hooks). Commit.
2. `devmemory checkpoint` — narrate the 19 steps scrolling by; Version V5 created, Entire checkpoint linked by trailer.
3. `devmemory serve` → **Overview** (timeline V1–V5, one REGRESSION), click **V5** → **Development Trace**: intent → Claude Code / claude-sonnet-5 → Entire checkpoint `01K…` → commit `a1b2c3` → 3 files, +48/−12 → 34 tests pass → status SUCCESS → analysis + recommendation. Every node clickable; "View in Entire" opens the checkpoint.
4. **Compare V4→V5** — real diff, metric deltas, test deltas.
5. Open **V3** regression → **Previous Attempts** panel already links it from V5's "related failures."
6. Back in VS Code, new Claude Code chat: *"how should I change token expiry?"* → it calls DevMemory MCP `check_before_change(files=["auth.py"])` → returns *"V3 shortened expiry to 30s → 6 test failures, REGRESSION. Recommendation: keep a refresh window (see V4)."* The agent avoids the known mistake **on camera**.
7. **Intelligence tab** (Databricks): regression leaderboard, "Authentication: 4 attempts, 75% success", file churn — `auth.py` is the hotspot.
8. **Restore preview** of V2 → shows the safety tag it would create and the exact working-tree effect; cancel.

**One sentence:** *"Git remembered what changed; Entire remembered why; DevMemory connected them to the result — and just stopped the next AI agent from repeating a bug we shipped last week."*

---

## 19. Documentation Gaps

1. **No `DEMO.md` / runbook** — the exact, rehearsed command sequence (incl. the Entire enable + attach fallback) must be written and kept current.
2. **Entire checkpoint intent extraction is under-specified** — docs assume `checkpoint.explain` returns intent; it doesn't in JSON. Our decision (read `<idx>/prompt.txt` from the ref) should be documented.
3. **No config reference** — every `config.json` key, every env var, precedence, and which are secret. Needs `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`.
4. **Databricks setup is hand-wavy** — needs concrete steps: Free Edition signup, serverless warehouse creation, PAT scope, the three env vars, first-run schema bootstrap, and the local-fallback behavior.
5. **Status/regression thresholds** — docs say "configurable, no hard-coded thresholds everywhere" but never specify defaults. Needs a documented default rule set (e.g. metric regression = adverse move > 2% or > 1σ of history; test regression = any newly-failing previously-passing test).
6. **Restore semantics vs `entire rewind`** — docs note they differ but don't give the user-facing decision guide. Needs a short "which restore do I want?" doc.
7. **Multi-checkpoint-per-version** is specced conceptually (ENTIRE_INTEGRATION §13) but the DATA_AND_API_SPEC schema has a single `entire_checkpoint_id` column — the join table needs to be blessed.
8. **Agent/LLM analysis provenance & privacy** — what leaves the machine, to whom, and how to disable. Needs a paragraph in a SECURITY/PRIVACY doc.
9. **Versioning/`--force` and history rewrite** — behavior when a commit is amended/rebased after a version was created (Entire remaps via `post-rewrite`; DevMemory needs a documented policy — likely: detect via `post-rewrite`-style reconciliation on next `checkpoint`/`status`).
10. **`examples/demo-project` spec** — the doc mentions a calculator; we need a defined feature set, metric sources, and the scripted regression.

1	# DevMemory ⚡
2	
3	**Development-Memory & Version-Intelligence Platform for AI-Assisted Software Engineering**
4	
5	> *Git remembers what changed. Entire remembers the AI-assisted development context. DevMemory connects those changes with test results, metric baselines, feature status, and previous attempts so that developers and future AI agents never repeat past mistakes.*
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 🌟 Overview
10	
11	As software development shifts to AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Antigravity), codebases evolve through rapid, iterative prompts. Standard version control systems (like Git) track code diffs, but fail to record:
12	- **Why** the change was made (developer intent / prompt)
13	- **Which AI agent** generated the code
14	- **What test results & metrics** resulted from the change (e.g., accuracy 89.2% -> 72.1%)
15	- **Whether the step caused a regression**
16	- **Lessons learned from failed attempts** to guide future prompt turns
17	
18	**DevMemory** bridges **Entire Checkpoints**, **Git**, **Databricks Analytics**, and **AI Coding Agents** into a single, cohesive development memory layer.
19	
20	---
21	
22	## 🏗️ Architecture & How It Works
23	
24	```
25	┌───────────────────────────┐      ┌───────────────────────────┐
26	│       Entire CLI          │      │         Git Repo          │
27	│ (Checkpoints & Transcripts)│      │   (Commits, Diffs, Stats) │
28	└─────────────┬─────────────┘      └─────────────┬─────────────┘
29	              │ Entire-Checkpoint: <id>          │
30	              └──────────────┬───────────────────┘
31	                             ▼
32	               ┌───────────────────────────┐
33	               │    DevMemory Engine       │
34	               │ (Regression Detection,    │
35	               │  Feature Health, FTS)     │
36	               └─────────────┬─────────────┘
37	                             │
38	     ┌───────────────────────┼───────────────────────┐
39	     ▼                       ▼                       ▼
40	┌───────────────┐   ┌─────────────────┐   ┌────────────────────┐
41	│ Web Dashboard │   │  MCP AI Server  │   │ Databricks Analytics│
42	│  (Port 8765)  │   │  (Claude/Cursor)│   │   (Delta Tables)   │
43	└───────────────┘   └─────────────────┘   └────────────────────┘
44	```
45	
46	1. **Entire Checkpoint Linking**: Every Git commit generated during AI sessions includes an `Entire-Checkpoint: <ulid>` trailer. DevMemory inspects this trailer to automatically fetch full transcript context, developer prompts, and AI model names.
47	2. **Regression Detection**: Compares incoming metrics (e.g. accuracy, latency, test pass rates) against prior baselines. Automatically flags regressions (>5% degradation or increased test failures).
48	3. **Development Memory**: Indexes all past iterations with SQLite FTS5. Before an AI agent attempts a new task, DevMemory provides targeted warnings about previous failed attempts.
49	4. **Databricks Delta Lake Sync**: Streams version records to Databricks for cross-project agent effectiveness evaluation and regression pattern discovery.
50	
51	---
52	
53	## 🚀 Quick Start
54	
55	### 1. Installation
56	
57	```bash
58	# Clone or navigate to your project
59	cd /path/to/your/project
60	
61	# Install DevMemory package
62	pip install -e .
63	
64	# Or install optional extras for Databricks and MCP
65	pip install -e ".[all]"
66	```
67	
68	### 2. Initialize Tracking
69	
70	```bash
71	devmemory init --name "VisionAI" --project-id "visionai"
72	```
73	
74	### 3. Run Pre-Seeded Demo Data (Hackathon Showcase)
75	
76	Populate realistic development history (VisionAI model iterations, regressions, dynamic TensorRT exports, and API auth errors):
77	
78	```bash
79	devmemory seed-demo
80	```
81	
82	### 4. Explore via CLI
83	
84	```bash
85	# View current status & baseline metrics
86	devmemory status
87	
88	# View chronological history
89	devmemory history
90	
91	# Compare version 2 and regression version 3
92	devmemory diff 2 3
93	
94	# Check AI context & regression warnings
95	devmemory context --feature "image-classification"
96	
97	# Full-text search across past attempts
98	devmemory search "learning rate"
99	
100	# List tracked features
101	devmemory features
102	```
103	
104	### 5. Launch Interactive Web Dashboard
105	
106	```bash
107	devmemory serve
108	# Open http://127.0.0.1:8765 in your browser
109	```
110	
111	---
112	
113	## 💻 CLI Command Reference
114	
115	| Command | Description |
116	|:--------|:------------|
117	| `devmemory init` | Initialize DevMemory tracking in current directory |
118	| `devmemory checkpoint` | Record a new version connecting Entire Checkpoint, Git HEAD, and metrics |
119	| `devmemory status` | View current version, completion %, and active baseline metrics |
120	| `devmemory history` | List version log with status badges and metrics chips |
121	| `devmemory diff <A> <B>` | Compare two versions: line diffs, metric deltas (+/- %), test pass/fail deltas |
122	| `devmemory restore <ID>` | Safely checkout target version code to a `devmemory/restore-v<ID>` recovery branch |
123	| `devmemory search <q>` | Full-text search across intents, agents, features, and analysis |
124	| `devmemory context` | Output markdown prompt snippet formatted for AI agent prompt injection |
125	| `devmemory features` | View feature health, version count, and evolution timeline |
126	| `devmemory serve` | Launch the FastAPI + Single Page Web Dashboard |
127	| `devmemory mcp` | Start Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for Claude Code / Cursor |
128	| `devmemory seed-demo` | Populate sample 8-iteration VisionAI project data |
129	
130	---
131	
132	## 📊 Databricks Analytics Integration
133	
134	DevMemory streams development metadata to Databricks Delta Lake tables:
135	- `devmemory_analytics.development_intelligence.development_versions`
136	- `devmemory_analytics.development_intelligence.development_events`
137	
138	### Databricks SQL Queries
139	
140	**Agent Effectiveness Comparison**:
141	```sql
142	SELECT 
143	    agent, 
144	    COUNT(*) as total_versions,
145	    SUM(CASE WHEN is_regression THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as regression_count,
146	    ROUND((SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'SUCCESS' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*)), 1) as success_rate_pct
147	FROM devmemory_analytics.development_intelligence.development_versions
148	WHERE agent IS NOT NULL
149	GROUP BY agent
150	ORDER BY success_rate_pct DESC;
151	```
152	
153	**Files Most Frequently Involved in Regressions**:
154	```sql
155	SELECT 
156	    explode(changed_files) as file_path, 
157	    COUNT(*) as failure_count
158	FROM devmemory_analytics.development_intelligence.development_versions
159	WHERE is_regression = TRUE OR status IN ('ERROR', 'REGRESSION')
160	GROUP BY file_path
161	ORDER BY failure_count DESC
162	LIMIT 10;
163	```
164	
165	---
166	
167	## 🤖 Model Context Protocol (MCP) Integration
168	
169	DevMemory acts as an MCP Server for AI Coding Agents.
170	
171	Add DevMemory to your `claude_desktop_config.json` or Cursor MCP settings:
172	
173	```json
174	{
175	  "mcpServers": {
176	    "devmemory": {
177	      "command": "devmemory",
178	      "args": ["mcp"]
179	    }
180	  }
181	}
182	```
183	
184	### Exposed MCP Tools:
185	- `get_project_status()`: Baseline metrics, current version, test health.
186	- `get_version_history(limit)`: Chronological iterations.
187	- `get_previous_attempts(feature, intent)`: Warnings about past failed approaches.
188	- `get_version_diff(version_a, version_b)`: Code diffs & metric changes.
189	- `get_feature_status()`: Feature health & evolution.
190	- `get_project_context(feature, intent)`: Markdown prompt snippet for AI agents.
191	
192	---
193	
194	## 🎨 Web Dashboard Preview
195	
196	The web dashboard is built using vanilla HTML/CSS/JS with zero heavy framework overhead, featuring a dark glassmorphic design system:
197	- **Overview**: Active baseline metrics, recent iterations, test health stats.
198	- **Timeline**: Interactive timeline with status badges and Entire Checkpoint links.
199	- **Version Detail**: Full session intent, heuristic analysis, actionable advice, tests breakdown, and colorized Git diff viewer.
200	- **Compare**: Side-by-side metric deltas with green/red indicator pills and full code diffs.
201	- **Features**: Evolution timeline per feature area.
202	- **AI Memory**: Warning callouts for regressions and prompt injection snippet generator.
203	- **Databricks**: Agent performance comparison table and Delta Lake schema browser.

14	class EntireAdapter:
15	    """Wraps the Entire CLI to extract checkpoint data and session context."""
16	
17	    def __init__(self, repo_path: str):

27	                capture_output=True,
28	                text=True,
29	                timeout=10,
30	            )
31	            return result.returncode == 0
32	        except (FileNotFoundError, subprocess.SubprocessError, PermissionError):
33	            return False
34	
35	    def get_version(self) -> Optional[str]:
36	        """Get Entire CLI version string if installed."""
37	        try:
38	            result = subprocess.run(
39	                [self._entire_bin, "version"],
40	                cwd=self.repo_path,
41	                capture_output=True,
42	                text=True,
43	                timeout=5,
44	            )
45	            if result.returncode == 0:
46	                return result.stdout.strip()
47	        except Exception:
48	            pass
49	        return None
50	
51	    def get_checkpoint_id_from_commit(self, commit_message: str) -> Optional[str]:
52	        """Extract Entire-Checkpoint trailer from a git commit message."""
53	        if not commit_message:
54	            return None
55	        for line in commit_message.strip().split("\n"):
56	            line = line.strip()
57	            if line.lower().startswith("entire-checkpoint:"):
58	                parts = line.split(":", 1)
59	                if len(parts) > 1:
60	                    val = parts[1].strip()
61	                    if val:
62	                        return val
63	        return None
64	
65	    def list_checkpoints(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
66	        """List all checkpoints via `entire checkpoint list --json`."""
67	        try:
68	            result = subprocess.run(
69	                [self._entire_bin, "checkpoint", "list", "--json"],
70	                cwd=self.repo_path,
71	                capture_output=True,
72	                text=True,
73	                timeout=30,
74	            )
75	            if result.returncode == 0 and result.stdout.strip():
76	                return json.loads(result.stdout)
77	        except Exception:
78	            pass
79	        return []
80	
81	    def explain_checkpoint(self, checkpoint_id: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
82	        """Get full checkpoint context via `entire checkpoint explain <id> --json`."""
83	        if not checkpoint_id:
84	            return None
85	        try:
86	            result = subprocess.run(
87	                [self._entire_bin, "checkpoint", "explain", checkpoint_id, "--json"],
88	                cwd=self.repo_path,
89	                capture_output=True,
90	                text=True,
91	                timeout=30,
92	            )
93	            if result.returncode == 0 and result.stdout.strip():
94	                return json.loads(result.stdout)
95	        except Exception:
96	            pass
97	        return None
98	
99	    def extract_intent(self, checkpoint_data: Optional[Dict[str, Any]]) -> Optional[str]:
100	        """Extract the developer's intent from checkpoint transcript or summary.
101	
102	        The intent is typically the first user prompt in the session transcript.
103	        """
104	        if not checkpoint_data:
105	            return None
106	
107	        # Check transcript user messages
108	        transcript = checkpoint_data.get("transcript") or []
109	        if isinstance(transcript, list):
110	            for turn in transcript:
111	                if isinstance(turn, dict) and turn.get("role") in ("user", "human"):
112	                    content = turn.get("content") or turn.get("text") or ""
113	                    if content:
114	                        return str(content).strip()[:500]
115	
116	        # Check prompts field
117	        prompts = checkpoint_data.get("prompts") or []
118	        if isinstance(prompts, list) and prompts:
119	            first = prompts[0]
120	            if isinstance(first, dict):
121	                return (first.get("content") or first.get("prompt") or "")[:500]
122	            elif isinstance(first, str):
123	                return first[:500]
124	
125	        # Fallback to summary or title
126	        for key in ("summary", "intent", "title", "description"):
127	            val = checkpoint_data.get(key)
128	            if val and isinstance(val, str):
129	                return val.strip()[:500]
130	
131	        return None
132	
133	    def extract_agent(self, checkpoint_data: Optional[Dict[str, Any]]) -> Optional[str]:
134	        """Extract which AI agent created this checkpoint."""
135	        if not checkpoint_data:
136	            return None
137	        for key in ("agent", "agent_name", "model", "assistant", "author"):
138	            val = checkpoint_data.get(key)
139	            if val and isinstance(val, str):
140	                return val.strip()
141	        metadata = checkpoint_data.get("metadata")
142	        if isinstance(metadata, dict):
143	            for key in ("agent", "agent_name", "model"):
144	                val = metadata.get(key)
145	                if val and isinstance(val, str):
146	                    return val.strip()
147	        return None
148	
149	    def search_checkpoints(self, query: str) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
150	        """Search checkpoints via `entire checkpoint search <query> --json`."""
151	        if not query:
152	            return []
153	        try:
154	            result = subprocess.run(
155	                [self._entire_bin, "checkpoint", "search", query, "--json"],
156	                cwd=self.repo_path,
157	                capture_output=True,
158	                text=True,
159	                timeout=30,
160	            )
161	            if result.returncode == 0 and result.stdout.strip():
162	                return json.loads(result.stdout)
163	        except Exception:
164	            pass
165	        return []
166	
167	    def get_impact_analysis(self, changed_files: List[str]) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
168	        """Use Entire Graph plugin to find affected modules if available."""
169	        if not changed_files:
170	            return None
171	        try:
172	            cmd = [self._entire_bin, "graph", "impact", "--files"] + list(changed_files) + ["--json"]
173	            result = subprocess.run(
174	                cmd,
175	                cwd=self.repo_path,
176	                capture_output=True,
177	                text=True,
178	                timeout=20,
179	            )
180	            if result.returncode == 0 and result.stdout.strip():
181	                return json.loads(result.stdout)
182	        except Exception:
183	            pass
184	        return None

1	"""GitAdapter for DevMemory using GitPython.
2	
3	Handles commit inspection, diff calculation, branch detection, and safe restores.
4	"""
5	
6	import os
7	from typing import Optional, List, Dict, Any
8	import git
9	
10	
11	class GitAdapter:
12	    """Encapsulates git repository operations via GitPython."""
13	
14	    def __init__(self, repo_path: str):
15	        self.repo_path = os.path.abspath(repo_path)
16	        self._repo: Optional[git.Repo] = None
17	
18	    @property
19	    def repo(self) -> git.Repo:
20	        if self._repo is None:
21	            self._repo = git.Repo(self.repo_path)
22	        return self._repo
23	
24	    def is_git_repo(self) -> bool:
25	        """Check if target path is an initialized git repository."""
26	        try:
27	            _ = self.repo.head
28	            return True
29	        except (git.InvalidGitRepositoryError, git.NoSuchPathError, TypeError):
30	            return False
31	        except Exception:
32	            return os.path.exists(os.path.join(self.repo_path, ".git"))
33	
34	    def get_head_commit(self) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
35	        """Get HEAD commit details."""
36	        try:
37	            commit = self.repo.head.commit
38	            parent_sha = commit.parents[0].hexsha if commit.parents else None
39	            return {
40	                "sha": commit.hexsha,
41	                "short_sha": commit.hexsha[:7],
42	                "message": commit.message.strip(),
43	                "author": str(commit.author),
44	                "timestamp": commit.committed_datetime.isoformat(),
45	                "parent": parent_sha,
46	            }
47	        except Exception:
48	            return None
49	
50	    def get_diff_stats(self, commit_a: Optional[str], commit_b: Optional[str]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
51	        """Compute diff statistics (files, additions, deletions, diff text) between two commits."""
52	        default_res = {
53	            "files": [],
54	            "additions": 0,
55	            "deletions": 0,
56	            "diff": "",
57	        }
58	        if not commit_b:
59	            return default_res
60	
61	        try:
62	            if not commit_a:
63	                try:
64	                    diff_text = self.repo.git.show(commit_b, format="", stat=False)
65	                    numstat = self.repo.git.show(commit_b, format="", numstat=True)
66	                except Exception:
67	                    diff_text = ""
68	                    numstat = ""
69	            else:
70	                diff_text = self.repo.git.diff(commit_a, commit_b)
71	                numstat = self.repo.git.diff(commit_a, commit_b, numstat=True)
72	
73	            files: List[str] = []
74	            additions = 0
75	            deletions = 0
76	
77	            for line in numstat.strip().split("\n"):
78	                if not line.strip():
79	                    continue
80	                parts = line.split("\t")
81	                if len(parts) == 3:
82	                    add = int(parts[0]) if parts[0] != "-" else 0
83	                    rem = int(parts[1]) if parts[1] != "-" else 0
84	                    additions += add
85	                    deletions += rem
86	                    files.append(parts[2].strip())
87	
88	            return {
89	                "files": files,
90	                "additions": additions,
91	                "deletions": deletions,
92	                "diff": diff_text,
93	            }
94	        except Exception as e:
95	            return {
96	                "files": [],
97	                "additions": 0,
98	                "deletions": 0,
99	                "diff": f"Diff unavailable: {e}",
100	            }
101	
102	    def get_diff_text(self, commit_a: str, commit_b: str) -> str:
103	        """Get raw diff text between two commits."""
104	        try:
105	            return self.repo.git.diff(commit_a, commit_b)
106	        except Exception as e:
107	            return f"Diff error: {e}"
108	
109	    def get_branch(self) -> str:
110	        """Return the active branch name or 'detached'."""
111	        try:
112	            return self.repo.active_branch.name
113	        except (TypeError, ValueError, AttributeError):
114	            return "detached"
115	        except Exception:
116	            return "unknown"
117	
118	    def restore_commit(self, commit_sha: str) -> str:
119	        """Safely restore/checkout to a commit using a dedicated recovery branch."""
120	        branch_name = f"devmemory-restore-{commit_sha[:8]}"
121	        try:
122	            self.repo.git.checkout(commit_sha, b=branch_name)
123	            return branch_name
124	        except Exception:
125	            self.repo.git.checkout(branch_name)
126	            return branch_name
127	
128	    def get_commit_history(self, limit: int = 50) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
129	        """Retrieve recent git commit log."""
130	        commits = []
131	        try:
132	            for commit in self.repo.iter_commits(max_count=limit):
133	                commits.append({
134	                    "sha": commit.hexsha,
135	                    "message": commit.message.strip(),
136	                    "author": str(commit.author),
137	                    "timestamp": commit.committed_datetime.isoformat(),
138	                })
139	        except Exception:
140	            pass
141	        return commits
142

1	"""
2	DevMemory — Development-memory and version-intelligence for AI-assisted software development.
3	
4	Git remembers what changed.
5	Entire remembers the AI-assisted development context.
6	DevMemory connects those changes with results, metrics, feature status, project state,
7	and previous attempts so that developers and future AI agents can understand the
8	complete development history.

13	import os
14	import tarfile
15	import json
16	from datetime import datetime
17	from typing import Optional, Dict, Any, List
18	
19	from devmemory.config import DevMemoryConfig
20	from devmemory.database import DevMemoryDB
21	from devmemory.models import (
22	    DevelopmentVersion,
23	    Feature,
24	    ProjectState,
25	    VersionStatus,
26	    FeatureStatus,
27	)
28	from devmemory.adapters.entire import EntireAdapter
29	from devmemory.adapters.git_adapter import GitAdapter
30	from devmemory.adapters.databricks import DatabricksAdapter
31	from devmemory.intelligence.analyzer import (
32	    detect_regression,
33	    infer_status,
34	    generate_analysis_and_recommendation,
35	)

41	
42	class DevMemoryProject:
43	    """Main entry point for the DevMemory Python API."""
44	
45	    def __init__(self, project_path: str = "."):
46	        self.project_path = os.path.abspath(project_path)
47	        self.config = DevMemoryConfig.load(self.project_path)
48	        self.db = DevMemoryDB(self.project_path)
49	        self.git = GitAdapter(self.project_path)
50	        self.entire = EntireAdapter(self.project_path)
51	        self.databricks = DatabricksAdapter(self.config)
52	
53	    def status(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
54	        """Get current project status and latest baseline metrics."""
55	        project = self.db.get_project()
56	        if not project:
57	            return {"error": "Project not initialized. Run `devmemory init` first."}
58	
59	        versions = self.db.get_all_versions()
60	        features = self.db.get_all_features()
61	        latest = versions[-1] if versions else None
62	
63	        return {
64	            "project_id": project["project_id"],
65	            "project_name": project["project_name"],
66	            "current_version": project["current_version"],
67	            "total_versions": len(versions),
68	            "latest_status": latest["status"] if latest else None,
69	            "latest_metrics": _parse_json(latest["metrics"]) if latest else {},
70	            "features": [
71	                {"name": f["name"], "status": f["status"], "latest_metrics": _parse_json(f.get("latest_metrics"))}
72	                for f in features
73	            ],
74	            "total_tests_passed": latest["tests_passed"] if latest else None,
75	            "total_tests_failed": latest["tests_failed"] if latest else None,
76	            "is_databricks_configured": self.databricks.is_configured,
77	            "is_entire_available": self.entire.is_available(),
78	        }
79	
80	    def checkpoint(
81	        self,
82	        intent: Optional[str] = None,
83	        feature: Optional[str] = None,
84	        status: Optional[str] = None,
85	        tests_passed: Optional[int] = None,
86	        tests_failed: Optional[int] = None,
87	        metrics: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
88	        errors: Optional[List[str]] = None,
89	        agent: Optional[str] = None,
90	        create_snapshot: bool = True,
91	    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
92	        """Record a new development version by connecting Entire Checkpoint, Git changes, and test metrics."""
93	        project = self.db.get_project()
94	        if not project:
95	            # Auto initialize if not done yet
96	            self.db.initialize()
97	            self.db.create_project(self.config.project_id, self.config.project_name, self.project_path)
98	            project = self.db.get_project()
99	
100	        # 1. Inspect Git HEAD
101	        head_commit = self.git.get_head_commit()
102	        if head_commit:
103	            commit_sha = head_commit["sha"]
104	            parent_sha = head_commit["parent"]
105	            commit_msg = head_commit["message"]
106	            branch = self.git.get_branch()
107	        else:
108	            commit_sha = "0000000000000000000000000000000000000000"
109	            parent_sha = None
110	            commit_msg = "Initial uncommitted / manual checkpoint"
111	            branch = "main"
112	
113	        # 2. Inspect Entire Context
114	        checkpoint_id = self.entire.get_checkpoint_id_from_commit(commit_msg)
115	        session_id = None
116	        checkpoint_data = None
117	
118	        if checkpoint_id:
119	            checkpoint_data = self.entire.explain_checkpoint(checkpoint_id)
120	        elif self.entire.is_available():
121	            # If no trailer in commit, check latest checkpoint from Entire CLI
122	            recent_checkpoints = self.entire.list_checkpoints()
123	            if recent_checkpoints:
124	                latest_cp = recent_checkpoints[0]
125	                checkpoint_id = latest_cp.get("id") or latest_cp.get("checkpoint_id")
126	                if checkpoint_id:
127	                    checkpoint_data = self.entire.explain_checkpoint(checkpoint_id)
128	
129	        if checkpoint_data:
130	            session_id = checkpoint_data.get("session_id")
131	            if not intent:
132	                intent = self.entire.extract_intent(checkpoint_data)
133	            if not agent:
134	                agent = self.entire.extract_agent(checkpoint_data)
135	
136	        # Fallback values for intent and agent if not specified
137	        if not intent:
138	            intent = commit_msg.split("\n")[0] if commit_msg else "Development update"
139	        if not agent:
140	            agent = "human-developer"
141	
142	        # 3. Compute Git Diff Stats
143	        diff_stats = self.git.get_diff_stats(parent_sha, commit_sha)
144	        changed_files = diff_stats.get("files", [])
145	        additions = diff_stats.get("additions", 0)
146	        deletions = diff_stats.get("deletions", 0)
147	
148	        # 4. Compare with previous version for regression detection
149	        latest_version_row = self.db.get_latest_version()
150	        prev_metrics = _parse_json(latest_version_row.get("metrics")) if latest_version_row else {}
151	        prev_passed = latest_version_row.get("tests_passed") if latest_version_row else None
152	        prev_failed = latest_version_row.get("tests_failed") if latest_version_row else None
153	
154	        active_metrics = metrics or {}
155	        active_errors = errors or []
156	
157	        is_reg, reg_reasons = detect_regression(
158	            current_metrics=active_metrics,
159	            current_tests_passed=tests_passed,
160	            current_tests_failed=tests_failed,
161	            previous_metrics=prev_metrics,
162	            previous_tests_passed=prev_passed,
163	            previous_tests_failed=prev_failed,
164	        )
165	
166	        inferred_st = infer_status(
167	            tests_passed=tests_passed,
168	            tests_failed=tests_failed,
169	            errors=active_errors,
170	            is_regression=is_reg,
171	            explicit_status=status,
172	        )
173	
174	        # 5. Snapshot artifact
175	        artifact_path = None
176	        current_version_id = (project["current_version"] or 0) + 1
177	        if create_snapshot:
178	            artifact_path = self._create_snapshot_tar(current_version_id, commit_sha[:7])
179	
180	        # 6. Build model instance for analysis generation
181	        dev_version_model = DevelopmentVersion(
182	            version_id=current_version_id,
183	            project_id=self.config.project_id,
184	            timestamp=datetime.now(),
185	            checkpoint_id=checkpoint_id,
186	            session_id=session_id,
187	            agent=agent,
188	            intent=intent,
189	            git_commit=commit_sha,
190	            parent_commit=parent_sha,
191	            branch=branch,
192	            changed_files=changed_files,
193	            additions=additions,
194	            deletions=deletions,
195	            feature=feature,
196	            status=inferred_st,
197	            tests_passed=tests_passed,
198	            tests_failed=tests_failed,
199	            metrics=active_metrics,
200	            errors=active_errors,
201	            is_regression=is_reg,
202	            artifact_path=artifact_path,
203	        )
204	
205	        prev_version_model = None
206	        if latest_version_row:
207	            try:
208	                prev_version_model = DevelopmentVersion(
209	                    version_id=latest_version_row["version_id"],
210	                    project_id=latest_version_row["project_id"],
211	                    git_commit=latest_version_row["git_commit"],
212	                    metrics=_parse_json(latest_version_row["metrics"]),
213	                    tests_passed=latest_version_row["tests_passed"],
214	                    tests_failed=latest_version_row["tests_failed"],
215	                )
216	            except Exception:
217	                pass
218	
219	        analysis, recommendation = generate_analysis_and_recommendation(
220	            version=dev_version_model,
221	            previous=prev_version_model,
222	            regression_reasons=reg_reasons,
223	        )
224	        dev_version_model.analysis = analysis
225	        dev_version_model.recommendation = recommendation
226	
227	        # 7. Persist to SQLite
228	        new_vid = self.db.create_version(
229	            project_id=self.config.project_id,
230	            timestamp=dev_version_model.timestamp.isoformat(),
231	            checkpoint_id=checkpoint_id,
232	            session_id=session_id,
233	            agent=agent,
234	            intent=intent,
235	            git_commit=commit_sha,
236	            parent_commit=parent_sha,
237	            branch=branch,
238	            changed_files=changed_files,
239	            additions=additions,
240	            deletions=deletions,
241	            feature=feature,
242	            status=inferred_st.value,
243	            tests_passed=tests_passed,
244	            tests_failed=tests_failed,
245	            metrics=active_metrics,
246	            errors=active_errors,
247	            analysis=analysis,
248	            recommendation=recommendation,
249	            is_regression=1 if is_reg else 0,
250	            artifact_path=artifact_path,
251	        )
252	        dev_version_model.version_id = new_vid
253	        self.db.update_current_version(new_vid)
254	
255	        # 8. Update Feature Table
256	        if feature:
257	            feat_st = FeatureStatus.IN_PROGRESS
258	            if inferred_st == VersionStatus.SUCCESS:
259	                feat_st = FeatureStatus.COMPLETE
260	            elif inferred_st == VersionStatus.REGRESSION:
261	                feat_st = FeatureStatus.PARTIAL
262	            elif inferred_st == VersionStatus.ERROR:
263	                feat_st = FeatureStatus.FAILED
264	
265	            self.db.upsert_feature(
266	                project_id=self.config.project_id,
267	                name=feature,
268	                status=feat_st.value,
269	                metrics=active_metrics,
270	            )
271

273	        self.databricks.sync_version(dev_version_model)

282	    def _create_snapshot_tar(self, version_id: int, commit_short: str) -> Optional[str]:
283	        """Create a lightweight tar.gz snapshot of the current workspace files."""
284	        artifacts_dir = self.config.artifacts_dir
285	        os.makedirs(artifacts_dir, exist_ok=True)
286	        filename = f"v{version_id}_{commit_short}.tar.gz"
287	        archive_path = os.path.join(artifacts_dir, filename)
288	
289	        ignore_prefixes = {".git", ".devmemory", ".venv", "__pycache__", "node_modules", ".pytest_cache"}
290	        try:
291	            with tarfile.open(archive_path, "w:gz") as tar:
292	                for root, dirs, files in os.walk(self.project_path):
293	                    # Filter out ignored directories in-place
294	                    dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d not in ignore_prefixes and not d.startswith(".")]
295	                    for file in files:
296	                        if file.endswith((".pyc", ".tar.gz", ".db", ".log")):
297	                            continue
298	                        full_p = os.path.join(root, file)
299	                        rel_p = os.path.relpath(full_p, self.project_path)
300	                        tar.add(full_p, arcname=rel_p)
301	            return archive_path
302	        except Exception:

335	    def diff(self, version_a: int, version_b: int) -> Dict[str, Any]:
336	        """Compare two development versions across code, tests, and metrics."""
337	        va = self.db.get_version(version_a)
338	        vb = self.db.get_version(version_b)
339	        if not va or not vb:
340	            return {"error": f"Version {version_a} or {version_b} not found"}
341	
342	        git_diff = self.git.get_diff_stats(va["git_commit"], vb["git_commit"])
343	        metrics_a = _parse_json(va["metrics"])
344	        metrics_b = _parse_json(vb["metrics"])
345	
346	        metric_changes = {}
347	        all_keys = set(list(metrics_a.keys()) + list(metrics_b.keys()))
348	        for key in all_keys:
349	            old_val = metrics_a.get(key)
350	            new_val = metrics_b.get(key)
351	            if old_val is not None and new_val is not None:
352	                try:
353	                    chg = float(new_val) - float(old_val)
354	                    direction = "improved" if chg > 0 else "regressed" if chg < 0 else "unchanged"
355	                    metric_changes[key] = {
356	                        "before": old_val,
357	                        "after": new_val,
358	                        "change": round(chg, 4),
359	                        "direction": direction,
360	                    }
361	                except (ValueError, TypeError):
362	                    metric_changes[key] = {"before": old_val, "after": new_val}
363	
364	        return {
365	            "version_a": dict(va),
366	            "version_b": dict(vb),
367	            "files": git_diff.get("files", []),
368	            "additions": git_diff.get("additions", 0),
369	            "deletions": git_diff.get("deletions", 0),
370	            "diff_text": git_diff.get("diff", ""),
371	            "metric_changes": metric_changes,
372	            "test_changes": {
373	                "passed": (vb["tests_passed"] or 0) - (va["tests_passed"] or 0),
374	                "failed": (vb["tests_failed"] or 0) - (va["tests_failed"] or 0),

1	"""Development version analyzer: status inference, regression detection, and heuristic recommendations."""
2	
3	from typing import Optional, Tuple, List, Dict, Any
4	from devmemory.models import DevelopmentVersion, VersionStatus
5	
6	
7	LOWER_IS_BETTER_METRICS = {
8	    "latency", "latency_ms", "duration", "time", "loss", "train_loss",
9	    "val_loss", "error_rate", "cost", "memory_mb", "memory_used",
10	    "failures", "response_time", "p95_latency", "p99_latency"
11	}
12	
13	
14	def is_lower_better(metric_name: str) -> bool:
15	    """Determine whether a smaller value is better for a given metric name."""
16	    clean = metric_name.lower().replace("-", "_").strip()
17	    return any(term in clean for term in LOWER_IS_BETTER_METRICS)
18	
19	
20	def detect_regression(
21	    current_metrics: Dict[str, Any],
22	    current_tests_passed: Optional[int],
23	    current_tests_failed: Optional[int],
24	    previous_metrics: Dict[str, Any],
25	    previous_tests_passed: Optional[int],
26	    previous_tests_failed: Optional[int],
27	) -> Tuple[bool, List[str]]:
28	    """Detect if the current development step caused a regression relative to the previous version.
29	
30	    Returns:
31	        (is_regression, reasons_list)
32	    """
33	    reasons: List[str] = []
34	
35	    # 1. Test failure regression
36	    prev_failed = previous_tests_failed or 0
37	    curr_failed = current_tests_failed or 0
38	    if curr_failed > prev_failed:
39	        reasons.append(
40	            f"Test failures increased from {prev_failed} to {curr_failed} (+{curr_failed - prev_failed} failures)"
41	        )
42	
43	    # 2. Test passed drop
44	    if previous_tests_passed is not None and current_tests_passed is not None:
45	        if current_tests_passed < previous_tests_passed:
46	            reasons.append(
47	                f"Passing tests dropped from {previous_tests_passed} to {current_tests_passed} (-{previous_tests_passed - current_tests_passed})"
48	            )
49	
50	    # 3. Metric degradation (>5% tolerance)
51	    for k, v in current_metrics.items():
52	        if k in previous_metrics:
53	            try:
54	                curr_val = float(v)
55	                prev_val = float(previous_metrics[k])
56	            except (ValueError, TypeError):
57	                continue
58	
59	            lower_better = is_lower_better(k)
60	
61	            if lower_better:
62	                # E.g. latency jumped > 10%
63	                if prev_val > 0 and curr_val > prev_val * 1.10:
64	                    delta = curr_val - prev_val
65	                    pct = (delta / prev_val) * 100
66	                    reasons.append(
67	                        f"Metric '{k}' regressed: increased from {prev_val:.3f} to {curr_val:.3f} (+{pct:.1f}%)"
68	                    )
69	            else:
70	                # E.g. accuracy dropped > 5%
71	                if prev_val > 0 and curr_val < prev_val * 0.95:
72	                    delta = prev_val - curr_val
73	                    pct = (delta / prev_val) * 100
74	                    reasons.append(
75	                        f"Metric '{k}' regressed: decreased from {prev_val:.3f} to {curr_val:.3f} (-{pct:.1f}%)"
76	                    )
77	
78	    is_reg = len(reasons) > 0
79	    return is_reg, reasons
80	
81	
82	def infer_status(
83	    tests_passed: Optional[int],
84	    tests_failed: Optional[int],
85	    errors: List[str],
86	    is_regression: bool,
87	    explicit_status: Optional[str] = None,
88	) -> VersionStatus:
89	    """Infer the development version status based on tests, errors, and regressions."""
90	    if explicit_status:
91	        try:
92	            return VersionStatus(explicit_status.upper())
93	        except ValueError:
94	            pass
95	
96	    if errors and len(errors) > 0:
97	        return VersionStatus.ERROR
98	
99	    if is_regression:
100	        return VersionStatus.REGRESSION
101	
102	    if tests_failed is not None and tests_failed > 0:
103	        if tests_passed is not None and tests_passed > 0:
104	            return VersionStatus.PARTIAL_SUCCESS
105	        return VersionStatus.ERROR
106	
107	    if tests_passed is not None and tests_passed > 0 and (tests_failed == 0 or tests_failed is None):
108	        return VersionStatus.SUCCESS
109	
110	    return VersionStatus.SUCCESS
111	
112	
113	def generate_analysis_and_recommendation(
114	    version: DevelopmentVersion,
115	    previous: Optional[DevelopmentVersion] = None,
116	    regression_reasons: Optional[List[str]] = None,
117	) -> Tuple[str, str]:
118	    """Generate concise heuristic analysis and actionable recommendations for AI/human."""
119	    reasons = regression_reasons or []
120	    analysis_parts = []
121	    recommendation_parts = []
122	
123	    # Analysis summary
124	    if version.is_regression:
125	        analysis_parts.append("REGRESSION DETECTED: " + "; ".join(reasons))
126	        recommendation_parts.append(
127	            "Do not deploy this change. Review git diff and investigate recent edits."
128	        )
129	        if version.feature:
130	            recommendation_parts.append(
131	                f"For feature '{version.feature}', revert or refine the implementation before proceeding."
132	            )
133	    elif version.status == VersionStatus.ERROR:
134	        analysis_parts.append("Execution or build errors encountered.")
135	        if version.errors:
136	            analysis_parts.append(f"Errors: {', '.join(version.errors[:2])}")
137	        recommendation_parts.append("Fix failing errors before committing further changes.")
138	    elif version.status == VersionStatus.SUCCESS:
139	        analysis_parts.append("All validations and tests passed successfully.")
140	        if previous and version.metrics and previous.metrics:
141	            improvements = []
142	            for k, v in version.metrics.items():
143	                if k in previous.metrics:
144	                    try:
145	                        cv, pv = float(v), float(previous.metrics[k])
146	                        if not is_lower_better(k) and cv > pv:
147	                            improvements.append(f"{k}: {pv:.2f} -> {cv:.2f}")
148	                        elif is_lower_better(k) and cv < pv:
149	                            improvements.append(f"{k}: {pv:.2f} -> {cv:.2f}")
150	                    except (ValueError, TypeError):
151	                        pass
152	            if improvements:
153	                analysis_parts.append("Metrics improved: " + ", ".join(improvements))
154	        recommendation_parts.append("State is stable. Proceed to next development milestone.")
155	    else:
156	        analysis_parts.append(f"Development step marked as {version.status.value}.")
157	        recommendation_parts.append("Continue implementation and run test suite.")
158	
159	    analysis = " ".join(analysis_parts)
160	    recommendation = " ".join(recommendation_parts)
161	    return analysis, recommendation
162

10	    if isinstance(val, (dict, list)):
11	        return val

13	        return {}
14	    try:
15	        return json.loads(val)

20	def find_similar_attempts(
21	    db: DevMemoryDB,
22	    intent: str = "",
23	    feature: str = "",
24	) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
25	    """Search previous development versions for failed or regressed attempts related to this feature or intent.
26	
27	    Provides early warnings to developers and AI agents to prevent repeating known mistakes.
28	    """
29	    warnings: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
30	    seen_ids = set()
31	
32	    # 1. Search by feature
33	    if feature:
34	        feature_versions = db.get_versions_by_feature(feature)
35	        for v in feature_versions:
36	            status = v.get("status")
37	            is_reg = bool(v.get("is_regression"))
38	            if status in (VersionStatus.REGRESSION.value, VersionStatus.ERROR.value) or is_reg:
39	                vid = v.get("version_id")
40	                if vid not in seen_ids:
41	                    seen_ids.add(vid)
42	                    warnings.append({
43	                        "version_id": vid,
44	                        "feature": v.get("feature"),
45	                        "intent": v.get("intent"),
46	                        "agent": v.get("agent"),
47	                        "status": status,
48	                        "is_regression": is_reg,
49	                        "git_commit": v.get("git_commit", "")[:8],
50	                        "metrics": _safe_json(v.get("metrics")),
51	                        "analysis": v.get("analysis") or "Regression or error occurred.",
52	                        "recommendation": v.get("recommendation") or "Avoid repeating this approach.",
53	                        "timestamp": v.get("timestamp"),
54	                    })
55	
56	    # 2. Search by intent query
57	    if intent and len(intent.strip()) > 2:
58	        try:
59	            matched = db.search_versions(intent.strip())
60	            for v in matched:
61	                status = v.get("status")
62	                is_reg = bool(v.get("is_regression"))
63	                if status in (VersionStatus.REGRESSION.value, VersionStatus.ERROR.value) or is_reg:
64	                    vid = v.get("version_id")
65	                    if vid not in seen_ids:
66	                        seen_ids.add(vid)
67	                        warnings.append({
68	                            "version_id": vid,
69	                            "feature": v.get("feature"),
70	                            "intent": v.get("intent"),
71	                            "agent": v.get("agent"),
72	                            "status": status,
73	                            "is_regression": is_reg,
74	                            "git_commit": v.get("git_commit", "")[:8],
75	                            "metrics": _safe_json(v.get("metrics")),
76	                            "analysis": v.get("analysis") or "Failed attempt detected.",
77	                            "recommendation": v.get("recommendation") or "Review diff before applying similar logic.",
78	                            "timestamp": v.get("timestamp"),
79	                        })
80	        except Exception:
81	            pass
82	
83	    # Sort warnings with most recent first
84	    warnings.sort(key=lambda w: w.get("version_id", 0), reverse=True)
85	    return warnings
86	
87	
88	def format_agent_context(
89	    project_status: Dict[str, Any],
90	    warnings: List[Dict[str, Any]],
91	    features: Optional[List[Dict[str, Any]]] = None,
92	) -> str:
93	    """Format structured development context into a markdown prompt block for AI agents."""
94	    p_name = project_status.get("project_name", "Unknown Project")
95	    curr_v = project_status.get("current_version", 0)
96	    tot_v = project_status.get("total_versions", 0)
97	    latest_metrics = project_status.get("latest_metrics", {})
98	
99	    lines = [
100	        f"### DevMemory Project Context: {p_name} (Current Version: v{curr_v})",
101	        f"- Total Development Iterations: {tot_v}",
102	    ]
103	
104	    if latest_metrics:
105	        m_str = ", ".join([f"{k}: {v}" for k, v in latest_metrics.items()])
106	        lines.append(f"- Active Metrics Baseline: {m_str}")
107	
108	    if features:
109	        done = [f["name"] for f in features if f.get("status") == "COMPLETE"]
110	        in_prog = [f["name"] for f in features if f.get("status") != "COMPLETE"]
111	        if done:
112	            lines.append(f"- Completed Features: {', '.join(done)}")
113	        if in_prog:
114	            lines.append(f"- Incomplete Features: {', '.join(in_prog)}")
115	
116	    if warnings:
117	        lines.append("\n⚠️ **DEVELOPMENT MEMORY WARNINGS (Previous Regressions / Errors):**")
118	        for w in warnings[:5]:
119	            lines.append(
120	                f"- **v{w['version_id']} [{w['status']}]** (Feature: `{w.get('feature') or 'all'}`): "
121	                f"Intent: \"{w.get('intent') or 'N/A'}\". "
122	                f"Advice: {w.get('recommendation')}"
123	            )
124	    else:
125	        lines.append("\n✅ No relevant previous regressions recorded for this scope.")
126	
127	    return "\n".join(lines)
